intended_object: Take a self-adjoint, possibly unbounded operator A on a complex Hilbert space H, with spectral measure E, and a Borel set B ⊆ ℝ. The object is the part of A in the reducing subspace E(B)H: the operator on E(B)H with domain D(A) ∩ E(B)H, acting as x ↦ Ax. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition just calls `specRestrict`. That operator is defined on `specRange`, the range of the spectral projection E(B), which the docstring says is definitionally `selfAdjointSpectralSubspace`. Its domain is `A.domain.comap (specRange).subtype`, the set of vectors of E(B)H that lie in D(A). On that domain it acts as x ↦ Ax. The library proves that Ax lies in E(B)H again (`apply_mem_specRange`), and that is all the codomain needs.

The spectral measure `spectralPVM` is built from the Borel functional calculus of the Cayley transform of A. This is the standard way to build the spectral measure of an unbounded self-adjoint operator. The result is exactly the textbook restriction of A to its spectral subspace E(B)H, with domain D(A) ∩ E(B)H.

The setting is complex Hilbert spaces with a self-adjoint `LinearPMap`, which is the natural one for spectral theory. Mathlib has no spectral measure or spectral restriction for unbounded operators, so it has no more general counterpart.
